labels.text: ## Walking tour Buenos Aires – Day 1
**START AT PLAZA DE MAYO:**
Let’s start your Buenos Aires adventure at the center of the capital city: Plaza de Mayo.
labels.reason: Directs traveller to start at Plaza de Mayo.

labels.text: This historic place is surrounded by **Casa Rosada** (presidential palace), **Catedral Metropolitana**, **Museo del Cabildo**, and the headquarters of the **National Bank**.
Plaza de Mayo was the center of the revolution in May 1810 where Argentina declares itself from Spain.
The actual independence was several years later.
In the center of Plaza de Mayo you find a small white statue.
Every Thursday grandmothers get together to remember the disappearance of their grandchildren during the military dictatorship in the 70’s.
In front, you will see Casa Rosada.
labels.reason: Points out a sight to look at.

labels.text: The presidential palace of Argentina.
Why pink?
That’s a powerful myth.
Some say it was a colorful mixture of red and white.
At that time the colors of both political parties.
Others say, there was no paint available.
So they took the blood of cows and painted the palace with it.
![Self guided tour Walking Buenos Aires](…)
Casa Rosada on Plaza de Mayo
There is more to see on Plaza de Mayo.
In front of Casa Rosada you will see a white building: Cabildo.
labels.reason: Points out Cabildo as a sight to see.

labels.text: Cabildo was used as the seat of the town council during the Spanish colonial era. In 1931 three columns were removed to build a new avenue.
Close to the Cabildo is Catedral Metropolitana.
It has a neoclassical facade with inside Neo-Renaissance and Neo-Baroque decorations.
Build in 1791.
Inside the Catedral you will find the Mausoleum of General San Martín.
labels.reason: Directs inside the cathedral to the mausoleum.

labels.text: General San Martín was an Argentine general and the most important southern leader of the South American struggle for independence.
labels.reason: Historical info about General San Martin.

labels.text: He is the national hero of Argentina.
The name San Martín will appear a couple of times.
**[Read here the why Jose de San Martin is popular in Argentina.](…)**
Also, the current pope of the Roman Catholic Church is an Argentinian.
The Catholic Church has still a lot of influence in Argentina.
Let’s move on during this self guided walking tour in Buenos Aires.
Go to the street Defensa.
labels.reason: Street walked as the attraction/next stop.

labels.text: The name itself explains what that street former was. It was literally the defensive line during a war against the British invasion.
labels.reason: Etymology and history of the street.

labels.text: Every Sunday Feria San Telmo takes place in street Defensa.
labels.reason: Directs traveler to visit Feria San Telmo on street Defensa.

labels.text: A hotspot on Sunday.
Locals are selling antiques, handmade products, … Continue walking and you will pass the first restaurants in Buenos Aires.
Local food, such as asado, empanadas, are here to find.
Wander around and enjoy the oldest neighborhood of the capital city.

labels.reason: Tells traveler to wander and enjoy the neighborhood.

labels.text: You will see that there not that much high apartment buildings.
It gives just that special character to San Telmo.
labels.reason: Descriptive comment about the neighborhood character.

labels.text: We going to make a small detour and go to the street Estados Unidos.
labels.reason: Directs traveler to detour to a street.

labels.text: You will feel the calmness of Buenos Aires.
This will maybe the quietest spot of the whole city.
On the corner, you will see Bar Sur. Well known for the tango shows.
labels.reason: Points out Bar Sur to see.

labels.text: Continue and cross the street Paseo de Colon.
labels.reason: Directs traveler to cross a street.

labels.text: You will see the first MetroBus infrastructure.
labels.reason: Points out infrastructure to see along the way.

labels.text: A fast bus system across the city.
In front, you will see a big building with columns.
labels.reason: Points out a building to see in front.

labels.text: Now the University of Buenos Aires department of engineers is there located.
labels.reason: Provides historical background information about the building.

labels.text: Before the building was destined to be the headquarters of Evita Peron’s foundation.
![Evita Foundation in Buenos Aires](…)
Evita Foundation in Buenos Aires
Let’s go back to the street Defensa.
labels.reason: Tells traveler to go back to a street.

labels.text: While walking you will pass the entrance of Mercado de San Telmo.
Jump inside.
labels.reason: Directs traveler to enter the market.

labels.text: Highly recommended.
The market went through a style renovation for the last years.
Trendy bars opened, but also you can still buy vegetables and meet.
[**Read here more facts about Mercado de San Telmo**](…)
Not far from Mercado de San Telmo is Plaza Dorrego.
labels.reason: Introduces Plaza Dorrego near the market.

labels.text: A cozy square in the heart of San Telmo.
Typical blue seats, bars around the square, and if you’re lucky you will spot the first tango dance.
Further, let’s walk on the street “Avenida San Juan”.
labels.reason: Tells traveler to walk on an avenue.

labels.text: A little bit to the right side there is the Museum of Modern Arts.
labels.reason: Points out Museum of Modern Arts.

labels.text: Walk up to Avenida Paseo Colon and take a right turn.
labels.reason: Tells traveler to walk up to an avenue and turn.

labels.text: Under the bridge, you see you a memory of “Club Atlético.
labels.reason: Points out memory of Club Atletico under the bridge.

labels.text: It was a clandestine center of detention, torture and extermination that worked in the city of Buenos Aires.
In 1978 the building was demolished for the building of the highway.
It’s maybe not the most beautiful memorial place.
However, it’s also part of Buenos Aires history.
Head back to the street Defensa and continue walking.
labels.reason: Directs traveler to head back to a street and continue walking.

labels.text: On your left side, you will see Parque Lezama.
labels.reason: Points out Parque Lezama as a sight to see.

labels.text: The big statue refers to Pedro de Mendoza.
In 1529, he went to explore South America at his own expense.
He founded Buenos Aires on February 3, 1536.
The legend says that Pedo de Mendoza put first steps on the ground where now Parque Lezama is. The coastline was in that time close to the street Defensa.
labels.reason: Mentions park and street as historical context.

labels.text: Take your time and enjoy the park.
labels.reason: Tells the traveler to enjoy the previously mentioned park.

labels.text: Make a stop at the national history museum.
Also located at the street side of Parque Lezama.
The entrance is free.
Across the museum, you will see Avenida Caseros.
This street is known in the Argentinian movie scene.
Walk on the typical red walkway and wander around.
labels.reason: Walk on walkway as part of route.

labels.text: Get on the public bus now. You can take line 29 or 152 with the direction “Boca”.
Or take a taxi.
(I prefer to take a bus or taxi because La Boca is a little bit too far to walk and also for safety reasons).
Let’s continue the self guided walking tour in Buenos Aires under the video.
[**SEE MORE VIDEOS ON THE YOUTUBE CHANNEL**](…)
Arrive at “El Caminito“.
El Caminito is Argentian most famous street with typical charm.
Houses are built with scrapyard materials in that time.
In the 19th century, it was the home of Italian and Spanish immigrants.
The colors vary because of the limit paint available.
All combination and mixes were more than ok. It’s a very artistic neighborhood and the area was tango was founded.
[**Read more about the founding of La Boca**](…)
La Boca is also the home of the same named football club.
**[Visit La Bombonera](…)**, the stadium of the football club.
The team colors are blue and yellow.
The myth tells us that they didn’t know to choose the colors of their team.
They made an agreement to take the flag colors of the first ship that entered the harbor at La Boca.
The first vessel arrived came from Sweden.
So simple can it be sometimes.
Visit La Boca during daylight.
Take a bus or taxi back to San Telmo.
I hope that you took the time to visit some museums and markets.
This is the heart of Buenos Aires history.
Enjoy your evening in one of the cozy beer bars or restaurants.
This was your first day self guided walking tour in Buenos Aires.
